key_agent_trends: Local-first agent runtimes are shipping for high-end Nvidia hardware, shifting privacy-sensitive and cost-sensitive workloads off the cloud while still escalating hard steps to frontier models.
Major cloud platforms are packaging vertical agentic solutions for regulated industries (legal, financial services) with domain skills, secure connectors, and partner agent ecosystems.
Open-weight models are being explicitly trained and released for enterprise agentic workflows—reasoning modes, tool use in live sandboxes, and coding harness compatibility.
Identity providers are treating AI agents as first-class identities with SSO, short-lived tokens, and centralized policy, replacing static API keys for agent-to-app access.

Specialized web-search infrastructure built for agent query patterns (high frequency, low latency, model-ready content) is attracting significant seed funding as agents become primary consumers of the live web.

stories.headline: Perplexity launches Portable Computer, a local-first AI agent on Nvidia DGX Spark and RTX Linux PCs
stories.what_happened: Perplexity shipped Portable Computer, a local-first version of its agentic Computer platform that runs model inference, orchestration, tools, and sandboxed execution on the user’s hardware. It launches on Nvidia DGX Spark and Linux machines with RTX GPUs (24GB+ VRAM), using Qwen 3.8 27B or Perplexity’s post-trained PPLX 27B, with optional escalation to cloud frontier models only after user permission. Local work consumes no billing credits; Windows support is planned for September. Connectors include Google Drive, Gmail, Slack, and GitHub.
stories.why_it_matters: Serious multi-step agents can now run primarily on-device for privacy and cost, with a controlled cloud offload path. This validates local agent harnesses for enterprises and power users who refuse to send sensitive files or continuous context to the cloud.

stories.headline: Google Cloud launches Gemini Enterprise for Legal and Financial Services with purpose-built agents
stories.what_happened: Google Cloud announced Gemini Enterprise for Legal and Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services, the first industry packages on its Gemini Enterprise platform. Legal ships specialized skills (brief drafting, citation verification, contract lifecycle, regulatory scanning, DSAR), connectors to iManage, NetDocuments, Relativity, DocuSign and others, and launch customers including Cleary Gottlieb, Freshfields, Weil, and Williams & Connolly. Financial Services includes a Google-managed Financial Research agent, 50+ domain skills, and design partners such as Deutsche Bank and CME Group. Both are in preview with data staying in the customer environment.
stories.why_it_matters: Vertical agent platforms with pre-built skills, secure system connectors, and governance reduce the integration burden for regulated industries. This marks a shift from generic enterprise agents to domain-packaged agentic workflows that law firms and banks can evaluate in production-like conditions.

stories.headline: IBM releases Granite 4.2 open models with native reasoning and agentic RL for enterprise agents
stories.what_happened: IBM released Granite 4.2 dense language models in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes under Apache 2.0, purpose-built for enterprise agentic AI. Models include switchable thinking/chain-of-thought modes, native tool calling, and 128K context (extendable to 512K). The 8B and 30B received agentic reinforcement learning inside live software-engineering, terminal, and search environments. IBM reports strong results on SWE-Bench Verified, Terminal-Bench, and math/science benchmarks. Weights are available on Hugging Face, Ollama, and other platforms.
stories.why_it_matters: Open-weight models trained specifically for multi-step tool use and coding harnesses give enterprises another self-hostable backbone for agents without relying solely on proprietary APIs. Native reasoning modes and sandbox-trained tool use lower the barrier to reliable local and on-prem agent deployments.

stories.headline: Keenable exits stealth with $26M Accel-led seed for web search infrastructure built for AI agents
stories.what_happened: Keenable, founded by former Yandex search lead Andrey Styskin and Amazon AGI scientist Matthias Petri, launched with a $26 million seed round led by Accel (with Conviction and other investors). The company has built an independent index of more than 100 billion documents optimized for low-latency, high-frequency agent queries, with an API and MCP server already used in production by AI labs and inference providers. Pricing targets frontier-scale agent workloads; features include model-ready content fetch and point-in-time historical search.
stories.why_it_matters: Agents query the web differently from humans—more often, with stricter latency and cost constraints, and needing clean context rather than ten blue links. Dedicated agent search infrastructure reduces grounding cost and latency and could become critical middleware as agent fleets scale.

stories.headline: Okta makes Agent SSO generally available, treating AI agents as first-class identities
stories.what_happened: Okta announced general availability of Agent SSO, bringing the open Cross App Access (XAA) standard into its core SSO product used by more than 20,000 customers. Supported AI agents are registered as identities in Universal Directory alongside humans, receive short-lived identity-governed tokens instead of static API keys, and are governed by centralized access policies. The capability is included in core Okta SSO plans at no extra cost; broader discovery and lifecycle features live under Okta for AI Agents. Partners cited include Anthropic, OpenAI, Salesforce, Atlassian, and others.
stories.why_it_matters: As agents gain access to enterprise apps and data, static keys and ad-hoc consent flows become a major risk and operational burden. First-class agent identity with SSO-style controls is a foundational governance primitive for safe multi-agent and agent-to-app production deployments.
